scenarios.title: Wider players' tunnel
scenarios.summary: The players' tunnel width rises from at least 4.5 m to at least 6.0 m, the top of the range the FIFA stadium book gives for the World Cup.
scenarios.rationale: Teams, match officials and medical staff need to pass at the same time on match day.

scenarios.title: Larger player medical room
scenarios.summary: The players' medical room rises from at least 50 m² to at least 60 m².
scenarios.rationale: More room for treatment, resuscitation equipment and the medical team.

scenarios.title: More accessible seating
scenarios.summary: The share of seats for disabled spectators moves from between 0.5% and 1.0% to between 1.0% and 1.5%.
scenarios.rationale: More spaces for spectators who use wheelchairs, with their companions.

scenarios.title: Larger press conference room
scenarios.summary: The press conference room rises from at least 200 m² to at least 500 m², the area in the World Cup space requirements.
scenarios.rationale: Larger media presence expected at the tournament.

scenarios.title: Larger team dressing rooms
scenarios.summary: Each team dressing room rises from at least 80 m² to at least 90 m².
scenarios.rationale: More room for squads and support staff.

scenarios.title: Longer back-up power
scenarios.summary: Back-up power must run for at least six hours instead of three.
scenarios.rationale: Covers longer outages and keeps broadcast and safety systems running.

scenarios.title: Clearer public announcements
scenarios.summary: Speech intelligibility in the seating areas rises from at least STI 0.55 to at least STI 0.60.
scenarios.rationale: Announcements must be understood in every part of the bowl.

note: Hypothetical requirement changes for demonstrating change impact. None of these has been announced by FIFA.
